data.cultural_impact: The name Shreya, in the Hindu culture, is believed to be derived from the Sanskrit word 'Shri', which symbolizes Goddess Lakshmi, who is the goddess of wealth, fortune, and prosperity. Names starting with the letter 'Sh' are considered auspicious, and Shreya is a popular name among Hindu communities in India and Nepal. Parents often choose this name for their daughters, believing it will bring good fortune, prosperity, and wealth to their families.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Shreya not only refers to material wealth and prosperity but also spiritual growth and inner riches. The name is a reminder of the belief that inner peace and happiness are more important than external material possessions. It encourages individuals to seek spiritual enrichment and respect for traditions, values, and dharma (duty). The name Shreya is an inspiration to lead a virtuous life, combining material success with inner peace and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shreya signifies the pursuit of happiness and success in life, rooted in noble values and virtuous actions. It embodies the journey to find meaning and fulfillment beyond material wealth.

vedic_reference.note: The name Shreya is derived from the Sanskrit word श्रेय: shreya, which means prosperity, wealth, good fortune, or happiness.

historical_references.reference: The ancient Sanskrit epic Mahabharata tells a story of a beautiful and virtuous woman named Shreya. She was the wife of King Yudhishthira, the eldest of the Pandava brothers. It is said that Lord Krishna himself chose Shreya to be Yudhishthira's wife, as she was the embodiment of dharma and was devoted to her husband.

Another reference to the name Shreya can be found in the Puranic scriptures. Shreya was one of the 14 gandharvas, celestial musicians who attended the divine court of Indra. According to the Bhagavata Purana, Shreya was so beautiful and enchanting that even the gods were captivated by her.
